newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN MAKES IT SEVEN WINS OUT OF EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN MAKES IT SEVEN WINS OUT OF EIGHT.

text.p: Australian Michael Doohan achieved his seventh success in eight races when he beat the Aoki brothers of Japan to win the San Marino 500cc Grand Prix on Sunday.
The defending champion, riding a Honda, pulled clear in the last eight laps after playing cat and mouse with Nobuatsu Aoki, also riding a Honda, in the middle part of the race.
Aoki finished second ahead of his younger brother Takuma, who recorded only the second podium finish of his career.
Doohan's victory, his second in succession on Imola's modified 4.93-km circuit, extended his world championship lead to a seemingly invincible 93 points over team mate Alex Criville of Spain.

Criville did not race on Sunday following his crash at last weekend's Dutch Grand Prix. He was not expected to compete again until September by which time Doohan may well have sealed his fourth consecutive 500cc crown.
The Australian made a poor start from pole position and did not hit the front until lap seven.
A lapse of concentration allowed Nobuatsu Aoki to pass on a straight during lap 15 of the 25-lap race but Doohan regained the lead three laps later and never looked like losing it a second time.
"I didn't make the best of starts and this isn't the easiest of courses to pass people on but I just decided to sit in there and pick them off one at a time," he said.
"Nobuatsu surprised me when he passed but I just sat on his wheel and tried to break his concentration. When I did get by him I just put my head down and tried to open up a gap.
Local favourites Max Biaggi, on a Honda, and Valentino Rossi, on an Aprilia, triumphed in the 250cc and 125cc categories respectively.

Biaggi's victory in a tightly-contested 250cc race took him back to the top of the championship standings ahead of German Ralf Waldmann, also on a Honda, who relinquished an early lead to finish fourth.
Biaggi took the lead on lap six but then twice lost it to Japan's Tohru Ukawa before breaking free from the field in the closing stages.
Ukawa, racing with a broken index finger after a crash in Friday's practice, finished third.
Teenager Rossi slipped back at the start but fought back to the front on lap six and stayed there to the finish.
He has now won six of his season's eight grands prix and heads the championship table by 47 points from Noboru Ueda, who finished fifth.
